mechanism_narrative: When the monthly FEDFUNDS rate rises by more than 0.25 percentage points over the next month, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return is expected to be negative due to expectations of tighter policy and reduced risk appetite.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25pp in the following month
regime_hint: early stage of a tightening cycle
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the identified FEDFUNDS increase, or FEDFUNDS rise is <0.25pp.

mechanism_narrative: An unexpected monthly increase in PAYEMS (labor market additions) of at least 50,000 jobs is associated with a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 trading days, reflecting optimism about labor market strength.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥50,000 in a given month
failure_condition: 5-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05) when PAYEMS meets the threshold, or the increase is <50,000.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained quarterly decline in GDPC1 (goods orders) of at least 2% followed by a rebound in the next quarter is associated with a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as the market anticipates a cyclical bottom.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 quarterly decline ≥2% then rebound in the next quarter
failure_condition: 60-day forward return is not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during the identified pattern, or decline is <2%.

mechanism_narrative: When INDPRO (industrial production) falls for two consecutive months below its 12-month moving average, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be negative due to supply-side weakness.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls below 12-month MA for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the two-month INDPRO decline, or the condition is not met.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in UNRATE (unemployment rate) below 4% triggers a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as lower labor costs are expected to support corporate earnings.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4% in a month
failure_condition: 60-day forward return is not significantly positive (p > 0.05) when UNRATE crosses below 4%, or the threshold is not met.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly increases in HOUST (housing starts) of at least 10% above the prior month's level are associated with a positive 20-day S&P 500 return, reflecting optimism about housing recovery.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by ≥10% month-over-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward return is not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during the two consecutive HOUST spikes, or increase is <10%.

mechanism_narrative: When PAYEMS falls by more than 20,000 in a month (indicating job losses), the S&P 20-day forward return is predicted to be negative due to risk-off sentiment in labor market weakness.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decreases by >20,000 in a month
failure_condition: 20-day forward return is not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the job loss episode, or decline is ≤20,000.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in RSAFS (retail sales) of 5% or more for three consecutive months signals a supply shock, leading to a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as consumer demand weakens.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decreases by ≥5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward return is not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the three-month RSAFS decline, or decline is <5% per month.
